These are projects which are semi-active and do not appear to have people directly responsible for them.

Dictionary

  
The dictionary project is now entirely subsumed by a combination of [http://www.lojban.org/jbovlaste/ jbovlaste] and [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/baupla+fuzykamni the BPFK] (or baupla fuzykamni). The rest of the discussion here is for historical interest only.

The [http://www.lojban.org/files/draft-dictionary/ENGDICT.ZIP draft Lojban dictionary] is online, compiled primarily by lojbab. It needs to have [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#lujvo lujvo] and [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#cmavo cmavo] added to it. Volunteers are welcome at all levels of expertise for [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#lujvo lujvo] definition work; there are thousands of words to be defined with more created all the time. [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Lojbanic+Community+Links Nora LeChevalier] serves as lead on the [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#lujvo lujvo] definition project. [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Old+Draft+Dictionary The set of working files for additions to the dictionary] are available online.

Eaton Interface

  
Helen Eaton's 1930s-era list of the most frequently used concepts in 4 European languages has long been a benchmark for completeness of the Lojban lexicon. Volunteers are welcome to translate one or more pages of words from this list to Lojban. The file [http://www.lojban.org/files/etymology/eaton.zip eaton.zip] contains word lists by page and proposed [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#TLI TLI] Loglan words for each concept (the [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#tanru tanru] metaphors for the proposed [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#TLI TLI] words are often very poor, but could spark ideas).

LogFlash 2

  
[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Lojbanic+Community+Links Nora LeChevalier] is working on a version of LogFlash for learning [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#rafsi rafsi] and [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#lujvo lujvo]-making. The prior version became unmaintainably obsolete in 1989.

LogFlash Language Learning research

  
lojbab gathers data from all Lojbanists willing to use LogFlash on a systematic basis for a few months. This data will help prove or disprove the meaningfulness of the recognition scores used to create Lojban [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#gismu gismu] and may lead to publishable general research in the field of second-language learning. Contact [http://www.lojban.org/llg/mailto:lojban@lojban.org lojbab] if interested.

[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#TLI TLI] Loglan Interface

  
If there is ever to be a reunification of the two Loglan language communities, the first step will necessarily be a translation interface mapping words and grammar from [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#TLI TLI] Loglan to Lojban (the other direction may also be desirable, but would be more difficult, and we intend to coalesce the community around the Lojban baseline in any event). The first step in this, a mapping of [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#gismu gismu] and [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#cmavo cmavo] , has been done, although there has been no accounting for [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#placestructure place structures] of the [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#TLI TLI] Loglan [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#gismu gismu] , and the work may be slightly outdated. See [http://www.lojban.org/files/draft-dictionary/Working/OLDLOG.TXT oldlog.txt] for the work that has been done.

Random Sentence Generator

  
This is being updated to be consistent with the baselined grammar. The existing program on this site dates back to grammar 2.08, about 8 years old. The update is low priority.

  
See also [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/random+sentence+generator the random sentence generator page on the wiki].

Textbook

  
Note that this project has largely been superseded by [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Lojban+For+Beginners%2C+The+Book Lojban For Beginners, The Book].

  
A [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Old+Draft+Textbook draft of the textbook] is available online, but it is out of date and incomplete. No one is working on it right now; it is considered fairly low priority until the dictionary is done. The main limitation in the existing draft is that a lot of beginner texts are needed which are both interesting and without use of esoteric features of the language. People tend to move beyond the beginner stage very rapidly once they start trying to use the language non-trivially, and few therefore end up able to confine themselves to the most basic features of the language.

Inactive projects (September 2014)

These projects do not appear to have been active for some time

----

Chrestomathy

This project is headed by [mailto:gregory.dyke@epfl.ch Gregory Dyke]. The goal is to produce a collection of translated and original writings designed to show a wide sampling of a language. We need translations of texts generally a bit longer than the typical effort (1000-10000 words), and as wide a variety of texts and styles, from as many different source languages as possible. Original works in Lojban that exercise a variety of aspects of the language are even more important.

----

Lojbanic Phrasebook Project

This project is run by [mailto:mugglesnsquibs@msn.com Robert Griffin], and the goal is to produce a Survival Guide to Lojban, based on the WW II language guides given the common American soldier. Presents a minimal vocabulary, based on common basic needs, to help in developing a small active vocabulary in Lojban. 
If you were stranded in Lojbanistan, away from the nearest English speaker this is the minimal vocabulary you would need to get by.

----

Newsletters

[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Jay+Kominek Jay Kominek] has been charged with producing a new issue of the [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#JL JL] newsletter for board approval. 
[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#JL JL] and [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#LK LK] will resume publication as soon as the [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-index.php?page=Frequently+Asked+Questions+About+Lojban&bl#LLG LLG] address data base is brought up to date. Changes and additions were recorded on paper for around 6 years without being entered onto the computer, and we are obliged to account to people for their money balances.

----

Monthly Announcement Project

A project send monthly announcements of general interest to the Lojbanic community. Headed by Jay Kominek.

----

xartum: The Lojban Internet Nation and Online Game

Those who make a nominal donation to the LLG would be mailed a naturalization certificate and/or passport. No proficiency in Lojban required. This would carry a membership in a text-based online storytelling and world-building game, although they need not participate to receive citizenship. The self-amending game process would develop a fictional setting to serve for Lojban what Star Trek serves for Klingon. This game might also involve the upcoming Lojban "MOO" persistent text adventure world. [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Matt+Arnold Matt Arnold]; when he is not writing [http://www.mightystudents.com/catalog/health_and_medicine%3Cbr%20/%3E medicine essays]; will be heading this up.

Project Report As Of January 1, 2006

I last updated the Wiki page "[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/xartum xartum]" on Tuesday. I have decided to wait until the Lojban MOO is usable before offering citizenship.

Project Report As Of February 4, 2006

Project Status As Of 18 Jan 2006

The following is from [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/xorxes xorxes]:

Completed ProjectsLojban Adventure

Nick Nicholas translated the text portion of the classic Colossal Cave text adventure game into Lojban several years ago. At the time there were plans to update an old Adventure program to support the new text, but the current state of adventure game design suggests that someone use the game engine called Inform (which has a specific manual for writing adventure games in translation). See the [http://mirrors.ibiblio.org/interactive-fiction/info/rec.arts.int-fiction.FAQ.htm rec.arts.int-fiction FAQ].

Update Late November 2002

This project has been completed with the help of a number of lojbanists. See [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/Colossal+Cave Colossal Cave] for details.
